title: Chat fragment anchoring and tokenizer compatibility matrix for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During onboarding of new open models we continue to see intermittent message boundary corruption in downstream chat templates (role delimiters shifted, trailing whitespace collapsed differently, and mismatched subtoken anchoring) which causes truncated responses or incorrect function-calling triggers. This ticket creates an explicit compatibility matrix plus a lightweight anchoring shim for chat fragments so we can guarantee template invariants during onboarding and publish a corresponding performance profile mapping.
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility matrix exists that lists tokenizer behaviours relevant to chat templates (delimiter tokens, whitespace normalization, common subtoken splits) for all onboarded models
A small runtime anchoring shim normalizes incoming prompt fragments to preserve role delimiters and predictable prefix/suffix tokenization without changing model inputs semantics
Unit and e2e tests cover: role delimiter preservation, stable function call trigger tokens, and no-ops for models already compatible
Performance profile publish step maps tokenization delta (tokens generated vs tokens expected) and updates the model onboarding doc
No regression on latency SLOs: anchoring adds <1ms median per-request overhead at p50 on standard microbenchmarks
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Audit — produce compatibility matrix CSV by running a deterministic set of template snippets across candidate model tokenizers and recording differences (script under /scripts/tokenizer-audit)

Phase 2: Shim — implement a minimal anchoring module in the onboarding pipeline that: 1) detects delimiter tokens per-matrix, 2) applies deterministic escape/unescape rules for ambiguous splits, 3) annotates request metadata with a tokenizer-compatibility tag
Phase 3: Publish — extend onboarding CLI to emit performance profile with token delta and suggested tokenizer_flags (eg preserve_whitespace=true, use_delimiter_uv="<<|role|>>")
Keep the shim opt-in via model pinning config (model_metadata.tokenizer_compatibility.policy = "shim-opt-in") so we don't change behaviour for existing pinned models
Implementation will be in two PRs: shuttle runtime change (anchoring library, lightweight) and onboarding CLI + profile publisher. Include feature flag in runtime for quick rollback.
testing_plan: Automated matrix-driven unit tests that feed canonical chat snippets and assert token boundaries match expected anchors
Integration smoke in the onboarding pipeline that runs the new audit suite against 5 representative models (one per major tokenizer family)
Perf regression suite: run bench harness on a dedicated CI shard measuring p50/p95 overhead and memory impact
QA: manual exploratory tests with function-calling scenarios and multi-part assistant messages to validate no change in behavior for pinned models
